newsitem.title: JAPAN: MITSUI CON MULLING THIRD-PARTY SHARE ALLOCATION.
newsitem.headline: MITSUI CON MULLING THIRD-PARTY SHARE ALLOCATION.

text.p: Mitsui Construction Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it may ask financial institutions to accept a third-party allocation of new shares to increase its capital.
The company, part of the Mitsui group, will also ask for support from financial institutions outside the group, Mitsui Construction Managing Director Susumu Naito told a news conference.
Earlier on Wednesday, four financial institutions in the Mitsui group, including Sakura Bank Ltd, said they would extend financial support to Mitsui Construction.

"Basically, we are not considering (asking financial institutions for) a cut in interest rates (on existing debt), although we are asking the four institutions to apply priority rates to us," Naito said.
A Mitsui Construction spokesman later stated that Naito used the word "cut" to mean a waiver of interest payments.
He said that, as of the end of March 1997, Mitsui Construction's own debts totalled 289 billion yen, while it had guaranteed 204 billion yen worth of loans for other companies.
